messages:
incident-bot: Paging: P0 - elevated GPU host errors in us-west1 affecting inference hosts > increased tail latency and token failures. Alert: node_reboot_count rising, pci_aer events spike. Pager: @mike (on-call) and @sara (sre) — please ack and triage.

mike: acked. jumping in. initial impact: ~6% of requests hitting error 502 from runtime, latency > 2s on tails.

sara: I'm looking at infra dashboards. I see a cluster of 4 hosts (gke-gpu-uw1-*) with repeated `AER severity=corrected` then ECC logs. Might be noisy neighbor or host firmware.

javier: tagging cloud provider support, sending a diag request. gcloud trace shows machine reboots at ~1790012200 for two hosts.

aria: customer-impact: traffic routed to hosted endpoints. Some customers reported bursty token errors and degraded throughput. Opening incident status page. set status: investigating. :eyes:

lee: runtime traces show kv-cache invalidations correlated with node handoffs. when node reboot happens, requests routed to warm-only nodes and token generation stalls for ~500-700ms then fails.

mike: mitigation idea: drain the affected hosts, route traffic away, and increase replica count for the autoscaler on the pool. can we do a quick canary rollout to fallback model on unaffected hosts?

sara: yes, start draining. I can set `kubectl cordon` + `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` for the 4 nodes. doing it now.

ops-bot: runbook step 3 executed by sara at 1790012355: draining nodes gke-gpu-uw1-12, gke-gpu-uw1-15, gke-gpu-uw1-22, gke-gpu-uw1-27.

javier: cloud support replied: initial packet shows repeated PCIe AER errors, then host kernel triggered watchdog and rebooted. They suspect a firmware/driver mismatch + noisy PCIe card. They asked for syslogs. I'm pulling dmesg from the hosts.

mike: share dmesg snippet here. keep sensitive data redacted.

javier: paste —
```
[ 1253.412345] pcieport 0000:01:00.0: AER: Multiple Corrected error received: ID: 0000
[ 1253.412350] pcieport 0000:01:00.0: AER: Device recovery successful
[ 1258.892001] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 79, pid=0, Graphics SM warp error
[ 1259.002112] mcelog: Hardware ECC error: cpu 3, mem-rank 1
[ 1262.546813] watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#3 stuck for 23s!
```

aria: that Xid 79 is GPU-related: memory corruption or ECC triggers. Customer side we should consider rolling to lower model sizes while infra is healing.

lee: hypothesis tracking: (1) noisy neighbor causing PCIe errors -> host kernel panic and reboot. (2) GPU firmware bug under certain PCIe loads. (3) memory ECC on host hardware failing. We'll add evidence flags as we go.

mike: I'm initiating a reactive routing policy: route 100% of new traffic to us-west2 and us-east1 pools for 10 minutes, and failover to cpu-backed fallback for non-latency-sensitive customers. Updating config now.

sara: config update in progress. `redwoodctl routing set --exclude-pool=us-west1-gpu --duration=10m` applied. Verified via planner: 98% of new requests are routed away.

ops-bot: Mitigation checklist: 1) Drain affected nodes (done). 2) Route traffic away (done). 3) Increase replicas in fallback pools (in progress).

javier: collecting more logs: iostat and nvme health look fine. The pattern: PCIe AER corrected errors escalate, then Xid 79, then ECC reported, then watchdog. Cloud says they will microcode-push update if we confirm repro.

aria: customers: posting status update to status.redwood.com - impact: intermittent 5-8% request failures and increased tail latency. ETA: working on mitigation and root cause.

mike: on-call handoff: @sara, I'll hand off at 1790012420 — you own next steps (deep RCA, coordinate with cloud, followup postmortem).

sara: taking handoff. I will capture timeline and hypothesis matrix here.

sara: timeline (so far):
- 1790012123 first PCIe AER corrected spikes on node gke-gpu-uw1-12
- 1790012190 Xid 79 on same host
- 1790012203 host rebooted
- 1790012210 routing hit slight error spike, autoscaler moved pods to other hosts
- 1790012355 nodes drained (manual)
- 1790012400 routing shift complete to other regions

lee: adding runtime evidence: sample request trace ids: r-0a1b2c, r-0a1b2d showing kv cache miss -> retry -> 502 after host reboot. attaching snippets in ticket.

javier: provider support asked for: full dmesg, `nvidia-smi -q` output pre- and post- reboot, and PCIe device tree. I'm uploading bundles to the support ticket.

aria: customer comms sent (short): "We’re seeing elevated errors and latency in us-west1 due to infrastructure instability. Traffic has been rerouted; engineers are investigating. We’ll update within 60 minutes"

mike: quick note: any sign of noisy neighbor VM on same host? gcloud shows external tenant with high DMA traffic on one of the hosts before errors. mark as high-priority hypothesis.

sara: hypothesis matrix update:
- noisy neighbor (evidence: increased DMA, AER before reboot) -> likelihood: high -> next action: ask provider to isolate tenant and confirm traffic patterns.
- firmware/driver mismatch (evidence: Xid 79 + provider logs) -> likelihood: medium -> next action: coordinate firmware microcode with provider.
- hardware degradation (ECC flags) -> likelihood: medium-low -> next action: request hardware health scan.

ops-bot: ticket created: RID-179001-INC / Support ticket #CLD-56421.

javier: cloud support responded: they isolated the noisy VM and observed lower AER counts on a test host. They scheduled a maintenance microcode push to the node pool tonight.

mike: good. next mitigation: schedule rolling reprovision to pick up microcode. plan to keep reroute active during maintenance window.

aria: we should capture post-incident actions: customer follow-up, RCA doc, include queryable logs for Xid and AER events, add a dashboard alert to detect PCIe AER rate > threshold, and revisit autoscaler behavior during host reboots.

sara: I'll author the in-incident RCA doc and include timeline + logs + hypothesis + followups. assigning owners: firmware followup -> javier, autoscaler followup -> lee, customer comms -> aria.

mike: thanks everyone. handing off formally. I'll be available if escalation needed. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: thread closed by sara at 1790012478: status moved to "mitigated (routing)".
